card.name: Words before world-scale or region-wide phrases
card.fires_on: Small words or gaps just before a large-scale geographic phrase such as 'in the world', 'countries', or a big area. Also some stray spots like 'al' in 'et al.' and 'Project' in 'Science Fair Project'.

modes.label: Before global scale
modes.description: A word or gap in a sentence about huge numbers or populations, where 'in the world' or 'countries' is likely next.
modes.example: Yet this is the case for billions<< of>> people around the world including many of us

modes.label: Before area comparisons
modes.description: A word just before a size comparison or place name for a large region.
modes.example: The area is roughly<< the>> size of New York State.

modes.label: Citation and title spots
modes.description: The word after a repeated title or in 'et al.' in a reference.
modes.example: Science Fair<< Project>> Encyclopedia Sandy River (Oregon)

card.writes: It pushes words meaning 'throughout' and 'entire' and holds back lists of countries or regions.
card.plain: It fires where the text is about to say something covers the whole world or a whole area.
